To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) thiol-based SAM containing azobenzenes are formed via two-step adsorption process, (2) dithiolane based SAM containing azobenenes are formed via a three-step assembly kinetics, (3) the H-aggregation on dithiolane azobenzene SAM is time-dependent, (4) photoisomerization in azobenzene thiol SAM is suppressed while reversible photoisomerization is clearly observed for azobenzene dithiol

(i) the assembly kinetics of AzoSH SAMs is characterised by two distinct adsorption steps, (ii) the assembly of AzoSS is characterised by three steps, (iii) H-aggregation in AzoSS SAM is time-dependent, and (iv) the photoisomerisation of AzoSH is suppressed, while the reversible trans-ciscis photoisomerisation is observed for AzoSS.
the formation of AzoSS on Au is characterised by three steps, while AzoSH is characterised by two steps.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of azobenzenederived SAMs on gold substrates, and the photochemical properties of these systems.
the formation kinetics and optical properties of azobenzenes in self-assembled monolyers (SAMs).

a fundamental study of self-assembled azobenzene-containing SAMs, which may be useful for a better understanding of the formation kinetics and related photoisomerization properties of azobenzenes in different environments, and may also provide useful insights into the design of new azobenzene-functionalized surfaces for a range of applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation kinetics of azobenzenes-based SAMs is a key parameter for the photoswitching capability of the resulting SAMs.
AzoSH SAMs are characterised by a very slow formation kinetics and that the photoisomerisation of the AzoSS molecules is suppressed by the formation process.
azobenzenedithiolane-based systems are more promising for applications that require reversible photoswitching than the azobenzene thiols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AzoSH SAMs are not good candidates for photoswitching, whereas AzoSS SAM are very promising candidates for photoswitchable surfaces.
the formation kinetics and aggregation of azobenzenemodified SAMs are very much dependent on the type of thiol linker used.
the formation kinetics and photochemical behavior of azobenzenes in self-assembled monolyers are highly dependent on the molecular structure of the anchoring groups.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the formation of SAMs with azobenzenoids should be performed in a controlled fashion, with a well-defined time frame, in order to achieve the desired properties for a given application.
the formation kinetics and aggregation of azobenzenes can be tuned by the nature of the terminal groups, which in turn affects the photoswitching behavior.
the photoisomerization process of azobenzenes can be tuned by varying the assembly kinetics.
